ambiguities.response: The premium base rate is $2.50 per $1,000 of insured value for standard cargo. This was set by the pricing committee in Q3 2024.

The route risk score ranges from a floor of 1.0 for well-established domestic corridors to a ceiling of 3.5 for routes traversing conflict zones or regions with poor infrastructure. The score multiplies the base rate directly.
Marine shipments attract a 15% peril surcharge, air shipments carry an 8% surcharge, and multimodal consignments bear a 12% surcharge. Road and rail have no additional surcharge.
The deductible credit is capped at 20% regardless of the actual deductible-to-insured-value ratio. Beyond that level, the actuaries determined that moral hazard outweighs the premium relief.
The insurer retains the first $500,000 of any individual loss under the excess-of-loss treaty structure. Losses above this retention are ceded to reinsurers proportionally.
The treaty ceiling is $10,000,000 (ten million dollars) per occurrence. Losses above this amount fall back entirely to the insurer unless a separate catastrophe treaty has been purchased.

The velocity check flags more than 3 claims from the same beneficiary within a 90-day window, but only when the total amount claimed in that window exceeds 200% of the expected loss ratio for the relevant cargo type. Both conditions must be met.

The claims assessment SLA is 4 hours from the moment of claim submission to the issuance of an assessment decision (approve, deny, or refer for investigation). This clock is paused only during sanctions holds.

The large-loss reporting threshold is $1,000,000 (one million dollars). Regulatory filings must be submitted within 72 hours of the triggering event (claim approval for claims, loss discovery for catastrophe events).
The full lifecycle of any claim must be reconstructable from the audit ledger alone within 5 minutes. This imposes stringent indexing requirements on the append-only event store.
A sanctions match at claim payment time triggers a mandatory 24-hour hold during which a compliance officer must review the match. This hold pauses the 4-hour claims SLA clock.

Claims above $250,000 require a senior adjuster who must provide an independent assessment before approval. Claims between $25,000 and $250,000 are assigned to a standard adjuster, and claims below $25,000 go to the automated fast-track queue.

The catastrophe loading is 25% applied on top of the base premium when a route passes through a designated catastrophe zone. A catastrophe zone is defined as any region with insured natural-disaster losses exceeding $50,000,000 in any single event within the past 5 years. The loading is applied before route-risk score multiplication, causing it to compound.

The loss-history weighting is: 50% for the most recent 3 years, 30% for years 4-7, and 20% for years 8-10. This is applied to the loss ratio for each band, not to raw claim amounts. Claims older than 10 years are excluded entirely.

Bordereau reports are due monthly by the 15th calendar day following the end of each reporting month (T+15). For example, January data must be submitted by February 15th. Late submission triggers penalty interest at 2% per month on outstanding reinsurance balances.
